input.question: if DNA is being damaged as you get older how can an old man, and there is cases of people with 80 years old or more, have a son and this son is like all other babies, new and fresh?
input.ground_truth: It's all thanks to a wonderful enzyme called telomerase. DNA gets shorter every time it divides, so it has long non coding regions on the ends called telomeres. These shorten too, but because they aren't essential for making anything they don't damage you until they actually run out. When producing sperm and eggs telomerase is active and gives each bit of DNA brand new telomeres even as the older people have telomeres that run out. Plants have telomerase activity at their growth nodes throughout their entire life, which is why when you take cuttings those are new and fresh too.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: if DNA is being damaged as you get older how can an old man, and there is cases of people with 80 years old or more, have a son and this son is like all other babies, new and fresh?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a big, old book. Every time you read it or use it, some of the words inside might get a little smudged or torn. That’s kind of like what happens to your DNA as you get older—some tiny mistakes can happen.

But when someone wants to have a baby, their body makes a special new copy of the book (the DNA) just for the baby. The body tries really hard to fix most of the smudges before making the new copy, so the baby gets a fresh, new book that looks almost like a brand new one! That’s why even if the dad is old, his baby can still be healthy and just like other babies.
